Nov 17, 2026

Configure a separate WAN gateway for each appliance in a high availability site

Cloudflare One ApplianceCloudflare OneCloudflare WAN

You can now give each Cloudflare One Appliance in a high availability (HA) site its own default gateway on a static WAN. Before this change, both appliances in an HA pair shared the same WAN gateway. Now each appliance can connect to its own Internet circuit, such as a different ISP for each appliance, with its own static IP and gateway.

  • In the dashboard, when you configure a static WAN on an HA site, enter the secondary appliance's gateway in the new Secondary gateway address field, next to Primary gateway address.
  • In the API, set static_addressing.secondary_gateway_address when you create or update a WAN. To remove the value with a PATCH request, set it to null.

The field is optional. If you leave it blank, the secondary appliance uses the primary gateway address, which matches how HA sites worked before. You can only use this field on sites in HA mode.

For details, refer to About high availability configurations.

Nov 17, 2026

Optimize original TIFF files with Images

Cloudflare Images

Cloudflare Images lets you optimize images for web delivery while storing only the original, high-resolution version. With Images, you can dynamically serve compressed and resized versions in the most efficient format for the requesting browser.

Starting today, Images accepts TIFF as an input format.

In publishing and e-commerce, TIFF is widely deployed as a master format for product photography, high-resolution scans, print assets, and archival collections. TIFF is a mature format, but it has limited support in modern browsers and tends to produce larger files than formats optimized for web delivery.

You can dynamically transcode original TIFF files to formats such as WebP or AVIF. These formats offer more efficient compression, which can reduce file sizes and improve page load performance. You can also resize each output without converting or modifying your original image.

For multi-page TIFF files, Images decodes only the first page. For supported formats and limits, refer to Limits and formats.

Nov 17, 2026

Investigate user risk events in a timeline

Risk Score

User Risk Scoring now groups risk behavior instances in a timeline. Each group highlights its trigger and shows later detections in time order.

Customize the date range to focus on the events you want to investigate. Select a timeline marker to view its events. The sequence helps security teams follow how risk events relate during investigations.

Switch to Table to return to the existing table view whenever you prefer.

User Risk Scoring is available on Enterprise plans.

For more information, refer to User risk score.

Nov 16, 2026

Artifacts now supports local development

ArtifactsWorkers

You can now develop and test Artifacts locally. Create repos, import Git repositories over HTTPS, issue repo tokens, and clone or push with Git on your machine before deploying to Cloudflare's global network. Local repos are separate from your deployed repos, so you can test changes without affecting production data.

Local repos also emit the same Artifacts events as production when a repo is created, imported, forked, or deleted, or when a repo token is created or revoked. This lets you test the Workflows that react to them before you deploy.

To use local repos when you run your Worker locally, add an Artifacts binding to your Wrangler configuration file:

Run npx wrangler dev, then use the binding the same way you would in production:

The returned remote points to your local dev session, so you can use it with a standard Git client to clone and push.

Local development requires the latest version of Wrangler and Git 2.32 or later on your PATH.

When you develop with npx wrangler dev, the Cloudflare Vite plugin, or the Workers Vitest integration, Artifacts bindings use the local simulator by default. To use your deployed repos instead, set remote = true on the binding.

To learn more, refer to Local development.

Nov 16, 2026

Cloudflare One adds Periodic Beaconing Traffic detection

Cloudflare OneGateway

Cloudflare One now includes Periodic Beaconing Traffic as a risk behavior. It analyzes Gateway HTTP traffic for regular check-ins to the same destination.

Cloudflare flags a user after more than 30 contacts to the same destination in six hours. Contacts must be evenly spaced, from 10 seconds to about 12 minutes apart. Few other users in your organization contact that destination.

Detection uses traffic behavior only. It does not use threat intelligence, categories, or reputation. Malware can check in with a command-and-control (C2) server this way, but legitimate software also checks in regularly. Treat each event as a lead to investigate, not proof that a destination is C2.

By default, the behavior is off and its risk level is Info. To turn it on, go to Risk score > Risk behaviors. Cloudflare reports a continuing beacon once. Events usually arrive 3 to 6 hours after the six-hour window closes.

Periodic Beaconing Traffic is available on Enterprise plans.

Nov 13, 2026

Browser Run Quick Actions now work in local development

Browser Run

You can now test Browser Run Quick Actions locally. Under npx wrangler dev, the browser binding's .quickAction() method runs against a Chrome instance on your machine. Before, .quickAction() worked only in remote mode, and local calls failed with The RPC receiver does not implement the method "quickAction".

Note

There are currently two limitations in the local simulation:

  • The json action is emulated. It requires an AI model to extract data, and the model is not available locally, so the action returns placeholder data that matches your schema.
  • The Kitesurf browser is not supported yet.

For details, refer to Test Quick Actions locally.

Manage AI Search instances in any namespace with Terraform

AI Search

Starting with Cloudflare Terraform provider ↗︎ v5.29.0, you can manage AI Search instances in any namespace, not only default.

The cloudflare_ai_search_instance resource has a new namespace argument. It defaults to default, so existing configurations keep managing the same instances.

You can import existing instances and namespaces:

The data sources read instances from the namespace you set:

When you upgrade to v5.29.0, review these changes:

  • The cloudflare_ai_search_instance import ID now includes the namespace: <account_id>/<namespace>/<id>. For instances in the default namespace, use <account_id>/default/<id>.

Nov 13, 2026

Set spending limits for Workers and Durable Objects

BillingWorkersDurable Objects

You can now set spending limits for Workers and Durable Objects to help control unexpected usage costs, or receive email alerts while your applications keep running. Support for more products is coming soon.

Use these controls alongside AI Gateway spend limits to manage compute and AI inference costs across your application. AI Gateway supports per-user and per-model budgets for Workers AI and other AI providers, applied to requests routed through your gateway.

Workers and Durable Objects limits apply across your account for the current subscription billing period. Each product has its own spending controls.

Set your limits and alerts

In the Cloudflare dashboard ↗︎, select your account and go to Billing > Spend limits. Choose a spending limit, notification email, and alert thresholds for Workers or Durable Objects.

For example, configure a $10 Workers spending limit with email alerts at $5 and $9. To receive alerts while your applications keep running, turn off Block usage.

See when a limit takes effect

The overview shows each product's recorded spend, alert thresholds, and pause status. Email alerts notify you without stopping usage. When a spending limit takes effect, Cloudflare blocks the product's supported operations.

To resume usage, raise the limit above current spend, turn it off, or remove it. Usage also resumes when the next billing period starts.

Usage reporting and blocking take time, so recorded spend can exceed a limit. Read about what counts toward a limit.

Choose alerts, limits, or both

For example, set a $50 spending limit for Workers and a $20 email alert for Durable Objects:

flowchart LR
    A["Durable Objects reaches $20"] --> B["Email alert sent"]
    B --> C["Usage continues"]
    D["Workers reaches $50"] --> E["Spending limit takes effect"]
    E --> F["New Worker invocations blocked"]

Set a spending limit with the cf CLI

Install the cf CLI and select your account, then run this command to set a $50 spending limit for Workers usage in the current billing period:

The amount is in US cents: 5000 means $50. To set a spending limit for Durable Objects, use --product-id durable_objects and update the name. Limits count usage already recorded in the current billing period.

You can also give this prompt to your coding agent. It will ask which product you want to manage and what spending limit to set, then use the CLI to configure it.

Use spending limits alongside budget alerts

The budget alerts introduced earlier this year notify you about account-wide usage costs without stopping usage. You can keep using them alongside the new product-specific spending limits and email alerts for Workers and Durable Objects.

To configure account-wide alerts, go to Billing > Billable Usage or follow the budget alerts guide.

Read the spending limits and alerts guide to learn how spending limits work and manage limits and alerts through the dashboard or cf CLI.

AI Search supports D1 databases as a data source (beta)

AI SearchD1

AI Search can now use a D1 database as a data source. AI Search runs a read-only query that you provide and indexes each returned row as a separate document. Scheduled syncs keep the index current as rows are added, changed, or removed.

Nov 12, 2026

Kitesurf is now open source

Browser Run

Kitesurf ↗︎, Cloudflare's browser engine for AI agents, is now open source on GitHub ↗︎ under the Apache 2.0 license. You can inspect the source, run it locally, and deploy your own instance to your Cloudflare account.

Kitesurf runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers. It parses HTML, applies CSS, executes page JavaScript, and renders screenshots without a browser container. It supports the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), so you can connect clients such as Puppeteer.

Kitesurf is still experimental and under heavy development. The team continues to improve web standards support, rendering fidelity, and performance.

Run locally or deploy to your account

Developers can run Kitesurf locally with Wrangler. After following the build requirements and setup instructions ↗︎, run pnpm run dev. This builds the engine and starts wrangler dev.

To run your own instance on Cloudflare, follow the deployment instructions ↗︎. Protect your deployment with Cloudflare Access or another authentication layer. Kitesurf does not provide built-in authentication.

Important

Kitesurf requires Cloudflare Dynamic Workers to create isolated Workers for pages. Dynamic Workers are part of the Workers Paid plan. A Workers Paid plan is required to run Kitesurf on Cloudflare. Local development uses wrangler dev.

Contribute and follow progress

Contributions and pull requests are welcome. The team remains focused on compatibility, reliability, and performance, with limited review capacity. Keep changes focused and follow the contribution guidelines ↗︎, including opening an issue and getting vouched by a maintainer before submitting a pull request.

Visit kitesurf.dev ↗︎, the main Kitesurf website and playground. Track Web Platform Tests (WPT) progress ↗︎ and performance benchmarks ↗︎ as development continues.

For background and technical details, refer to the introductory blog post ↗︎ and the Kitesurf update ↗︎. To use Kitesurf through Browser Run, refer to the Kitesurf documentation.

Nov 12, 2026

Export D1 databases with virtual tables

D1

You can now export a D1 database that contains virtual tables, such as full-text search tables using SQLite's FTS5 module ↗︎ or spatial index tables using the R*Tree module. Previously, export failed for any database containing virtual tables.

To include virtual tables in the dump, set dump_options.compatibility to sqlite3_cli_only on the D1 export API. The same option is available as the --compatibility flag on wrangler d1 export.

Import is not supported

This dump targets the SQLite CLI only. You cannot import it back into D1. Use the standard export for databases without virtual tables.

For more information, refer to Export a D1 database with virtual tables.

Nov 12, 2026

Set custom validity windows for RealtimeKit auth tokens

Realtime

RealtimeKit auth tokens now support custom validity windows, and you can revoke a single token. When your backend adds a participant to a meeting, it gets back an auth token that the participant's app uses to join.

Previously, every token was valid for 100 days from the moment it was issued. Now you can choose when a token starts and stops working, for example only during a scheduled class or interview, so a shared link stops working once the session is over. Pass not_before and expires_on in the token object when you add a participant:

Required API token permissions

At least one of the following token permissions is required:
  • Realtime Admin
  • Realtime

Both fields are optional, so existing integrations keep getting 100-day tokens.

You can also revoke a single token without setting the whole meeting to INACTIVE. If the participant is in the meeting, RealtimeKit removes them. A revoked token can take up to 60 seconds to stop working everywhere, so delete the participant instead if you need to block them immediately.

RealtimeKit rejects expired, not yet valid, and revoked tokens before the participant enters the meeting, so you are not billed for them.

Learn more

  • Token validity and refresh
  • Revoke tokens
  • Add participant API
  • Refresh participant token API
Nov 12, 2026

Add noise cancellation to web apps built on RealtimeKit

Realtime

You can now add noise cancellation to RealtimeKit web apps with the new @cloudflare/realtimekit-noise-cancellation package. RealtimeKit is a high-level SDK for adding real-time audio and video components, such as video meetings, to your web or mobile app.

Install the package:

npm i @cloudflare/realtimekit-noise-cancellation
yarn add @cloudflare/realtimekit-noise-cancellation
pnpm add @cloudflare/realtimekit-noise-cancellation
bun add @cloudflare/realtimekit-noise-cancellation

After you initialize the meeting, pass it to init():

How it works

  • Filters background noise in the participant's browser, before their audio is sent to the meeting.
  • Turns on automatically after init(), as soon as the participant's microphone is on.
  • Keeps running through mute, unmute, and reconnects, and cleans up when the participant leaves.
  • Never unmutes the microphone.

Noise cancellation works in React, Angular, and JavaScript apps on Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari, including mobile browsers. The RealtimeKit iOS and Android SDKs do not yet support it.

Learn more

  • Noise Cancellation: setup for React, Angular, and JavaScript, plus the full API
  • Noise cancellation example ↗︎: RealtimeKit's default meeting UI with noise cancellation turned on, also available in Angular and HTML in the same repository
  • RealtimeKit release notes

sha512() SHA-512 64 bytes

Nov 12, 2026

Cloudflare Tunnel extends URL normalization

Cloudflare TunnelCloudflare Tunnel for SASE

Starting from version 2026.11.0, Cloudflare Tunnel extends the URL normalization introduced in 2026.10.0. Normalization now handles semicolon-delimited path parameters before matching ingress rules. This improves security for tunnels with rules that require Cloudflare Access validation. The URL path sent to your origin stays the same.

Starting 2027-02-08, new cloudflared releases will turn on URL normalization by default. This replaces the previously announced date of 2027-01-25, giving you time to test the updated behavior. Upgrade to version 2026.11.0 or later and test your path-based routing before that date, including rules that match paths containing semicolons. Configurations without rules requiring Access validation are unaffected.

This setting is currently off by default. To turn it on, run:

Alternatively, set TUNNEL_DISABLE_PATH_NORMALIZATION=false on each cloudflared replica and restart it.

For more information, refer to ingress matching and Access validation at the origin.

Nov 12, 2026

EmbeddingGemma 2 now available on Workers AI

Workers AI

@cf/google/embeddinggemma-2 is now available on Workers AI. EmbeddingGemma 2 is an open multimodal embedding model from Google DeepMind. It maps text (including code), images, video, and audio into a single 768-dimensional vector space, so you can search a mixed collection of products, documents, and media with one text query.

Key capabilities:

  • Multimodal: Embed text, images, video, audio, or any combination of them in one input. Every embedding shares the same vector space.
  • Multilingual and code: Understands more than 100 languages and improves code retrieval over the original EmbeddingGemma.
  • Flexible dimensions: Set dimensions to 128, 256, or 512 to return shorter vectors and reduce storage, with a small cost to quality.
  • Long context: An 8,192 token context window, shared across all content in an input.
  • Task prefixes: Add short instructions such as task: search result | query: ... to tune embeddings for search, classification, clustering, or similarity.

Send text with input. Send images, video, and audio as base64 data URIs in messages:

Pricing is $0.0017 per million input tokens.

For more information, refer to the EmbeddingGemma 2 model page and pricing.

Nov 12, 2026

Inkling 2 Small now available on Workers AI

Workers AI

@cf/thinkingmachines/inkling-2-small is now available on Workers AI. Inkling 2 Small is the second generation of Inkling models from Thinking Machines Lab, and the first frontier open model from a US lab on Workers AI.

Inkling 2 Small is more capable than the previous generation. It is a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 594B total parameters and 18B active parameters. Thinking Machines trained it much faster than previous models because of improvements to their pre-training and infrastructure.

Inkling 2 Small works well for:

  • Agentic coding: Plan, write, and edit code across multi-step tasks.
  • Vision understanding: Interpret images sent alongside text in the same request.
  • General agentic knowledge work: Research, analyze, and act on information with tools.

Key capabilities:

  • Vision: Accepts text and image inputs.
  • Reasoning: Reasoning is on by default at high effort. Set reasoning_effort to max, medium, low, or minimal to change the effort, or to none to turn reasoning off.
  • Function calling: Build agents that invoke tools and APIs across multiple conversation turns.
  • Long context: A full 1,048,576 token context window.

Inkling 2 Small requires the Workers Paid plan or prepaid AI Gateway credits. The default rate limit is 20 requests per minute with standard Workers AI billing and 50 requests per minute with prepaid AI Gateway credits. For details, refer to limits.

Use Inkling 2 Small through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()), the REST API, the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or AI Gateway.

For more information, refer to the Inkling 2 Small model page and pricing.

Nov 11, 2026

GitHub automatically detects leaked Access service tokens

AccessCloudflare One

GitHub secret scanning automatically detects Cloudflare Access service token secrets exposed in public repositories and reports them to Cloudflare. Access then disables the affected token and emails account administrators.

Other secret scanning tools can identify Access service tokens using their consistent Client Secret format: cfast_, followed by 40 alphanumeric characters and an eight-character hexadecimal checksum. For tools that support custom detection rules, use this regular expression to find possible secrets:

This pattern applies to Client Secrets created on or after August 26, 2026, not legacy 64-character hexadecimal secrets. Matching the pattern does not validate the checksum or confirm that the secret is active. For details, refer to Client Secret format.

Recover a leaked service token

Before you can re-enable a leaked token, you must rotate its secret.

Leaked secrets do not support a rotation grace period. When you rotate one, the previous secret is discarded immediately. Update your services with the new secret, then re-enable the token.

For API rotations, omit previous_client_secret_expires_at. A future expiration returns 400. Attempting to re-enable the token before rotation returns 409.

For recovery steps and leak metadata fields, refer to Recover a leaked service token.

Nov 11, 2026

Improved Request Routing to Durable Objects

Durable Objects

Cloudflare has reduced the number of round trips needed to connect to a Durable Object when a location lookup follows a forwarding record to another data center.

When an object's destination isn't cached in Cloudflare's network, the first data center contacted may have a forwarding record pointing to another data center.

Previously, the first data center acquired a connection to the object at the destination and proxied it back to the caller. The caller then established its own direct connection to the object.

Now, the first data center returns the destination directly, without first acquiring a connection to the object. The caller then establishes a direct connection, avoiding the intermediate connection and duplicate acquisition.

Skipping this intermediate connection can reduce p99 connection latency for these relocation-related requests. Actual results depend on your workload and traffic patterns.

No code or configuration changes are required to benefit from this improvement.

To learn more about how Workers connect to Durable Objects, refer to Durable Object namespaces.

Nov 11, 2026

Hyperdrive raises limits for connections and configurations

Hyperdrive

Customers on a Workers Paid plan can now create up to 100 Hyperdrive configurations, up from 25, and configure up to 1,500 origin database connections per configuration, up from 100.

Configuration limit

The configuration limit is the maximum number of Hyperdrive configurations you can create per account. Workers Paid customers can now create up to 100 configurations, allowing more workloads to take advantage of connection pooling and query caching across different databases.

Origin connection limit

The origin connection limit is the maximum number of database connections that Hyperdrive can make to your origin database per configuration. Workers Paid customers can now configure up to 1,500 origin connections, increasing the connection pool size available for workloads that need more concurrent database access. You can configure this value via the dashboard, Wrangler, or the REST API.

We recommend setting the origin connection limit lower than your origin database's connection limit.

For more information, refer to Hyperdrive limits and Tune connection pooling.

Nov 11, 2026

Add a collaborative whiteboard to meetings built on RealtimeKit

Realtime

You can now add a collaborative whiteboard to RealtimeKit meetings with the Whiteboard plugin, which Cloudflare hosts and runs for you. RealtimeKit provides SDKs for running live audio and video meetings in your app. Many companies use it today to run online education and interview platforms, where participants often need a shared whiteboard to work through ideas together.

You add the Whiteboard plugin with the same plugins API you use for your own plugins. Load it in an iframe, with the participant's auth token after # in the URL:

Then pass whiteboardElement as the plugin's component when you initialize the SDK. The Whiteboard plugin guide has the registration code for web, Android, iOS, and React Native.

You can also build your own plugins and render them alongside the meeting UI. A whiteboard you build yourself needs a server that sends every stroke to every participant, saves the board between sessions, and checks who can open it. With the Whiteboard plugin, Cloudflare runs all of that for you.

How it works

  • Participants draw shapes, arrows, freehand strokes, and text on one shared board, and see each other's cursors and names.
  • Each meeting has one board. It stays the same across sessions, so participants pick up where they left off.
  • The plugin checks each participant's auth token, so only participants in the meeting can open its board.
  • It works on any domain, and you do not need to register your app's origin.

Learn more

  • Add the Whiteboard plugin: setup for web and mobile, permissions, and board data
  • Plugins: register, activate, and listen to plugins
  • Build your own plugin
  • RealtimeKit quickstart
